intended_object: The compression (restriction) Q|_{H_g} of the orthogonal projection Q onto V to the generic part H_g = (U∩V ⊕ U∩V^⊥ ⊕ U^⊥∩V ⊕ U^⊥∩V^⊥)^⊥ of Halmos' two-subspace decomposition. H_g reduces Q, so the restriction is an operator on H_g. Inferred from the docstring, the name and its use in the two-projection classification structure.
explanation: I read the body and the definitions it relies on. `halmosGenericPart U V` is the orthogonal complement of the sum of the four subspaces U⊓V, U⊓Vᗮ, Uᗮ⊓V and Uᗮ⊓Vᗮ. That is exactly Halmos' generic part. `restrictToInvariant` composes the operator with the inclusion of the subspace and restricts the codomain back to the subspace, which is the standard restriction to an invariant subspace. The invariance it needs comes from the lemma `projection_right_reduces_halmosGenericPart`. So the definition gives the restriction of P_V to the generic part, as intended. The one restriction of generality is the scalar field: the file works over ℂ, while the underlying Halmos file is stated over any `RCLike` field. Halmos' two-projection theory is classically set in complex Hilbert spaces, and this file is the ℂ-specific operator classification, part of the spectral and direct-integral treatment. This definition is just one piece of that classification, so I do not count the choice of ℂ as `too_narrow`. Mathlib has no dedicated counterpart for the Halmos generic part or for restricting projections to it.
